A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IPAD. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector evaluations, ablations, prompt-reconstruction experiments, linguistic analyses, and a ten-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of the combined detector, additional datasets and comparisons, expanded ablations, and retained human-assessment results.

M1.justification: V1 presents PTCV and RC as alternative distinguishers producing yes/no decisions. V2 adds normalized probability outputs and combines both distinguishers through a weighted ensemble, with weight 0.45 and threshold 0.54 selected on validation data. This changes the final inference procedure.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands to LongWriter, Code-Feedback, Math, and PubMedQA, adding long-form, coding, mathematical, and biomedical coverage. Appendix F also introduces back-translation attack scenarios. The original training datasets and existing XSum/Writing coverage are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds DetectLLM (NPR) and Binoculars to the existing OOD and attack comparisons; the earlier LRR comparator is retained as DetectLLM (LRR). Appendix F adds detector-level comparisons with published DPIC (ChatGPT) and DPIC (Vicuna-7B) results. Table 6 also consolidates two ChatGPT prompt comparators into one.

E3.justification: V2 drops F1 reporting, uses AUROC for the expanded ablations, and introduces validation-based ensemble selection. Structured datasets are evaluated using MachineRec alone because they lack human-written references. Appendix F specifies new 200-example datasets, three generators, and generation/attack procedures.

E4.justification: V1's input-only and prompt-only ablation expands into comparisons of individual distinguishers and the full ensemble across in-distribution, OOD, and attacked settings (v2 Figure 3). V2 adds DPIC attack tests and prompt-inversion examples. The linguistic statistics remain, but their original illustrative examples are removed.

E5.justification: The linguistic analysis retains the same significance reporting, including p-values below 0.05. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or seed reporting. V2's new classifier probability scores are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main detection results are extensively replaced: v1 Table 4 reports separate PTCV/RC OOD averages of 95.52/95.65 AUROC, whereas v2 Table 2 reports 99.38 for the revised ensemble. V2 adds structured-data results averaging 95.27 MachineRec and DPIC comparison results. These involve changed methods/protocols; prompt-reconstruction similarity scores and participant ratings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal probability and ensemble-score definitions and an inference-complexity argument in Section 2.2. The existing AUROC formula is relocated from Appendix A to Appendix C without substantive revision; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from two alternative distinguishers, emphasizing RC's superiority, to integrated dual-consistency detection. V2 adds structured-prompt robustness claims and revises headline advantages to 9.05% Average Recall, 12.93% OOD AUROC, and 5.48% attacked-data AUROC.

C2.justification: V1 explains robustness through RC's global matching versus PTCV's local alignment; v2 emphasizes complementary modules supporting fusion. V2 adds a substantive comparison with DPIC's embedding-based mechanism and replaces the deferred training-diversity limitation with computational-cost tradeoffs. The limitation concerning reconstruction of in-context examples remains.

D1.justification: V2 reports fusion hyperparameters, an inference algorithm, additional generator identifiers, and V100 deployment information; RC training time changes from four to nine hours. Code changes from promised to reported available, and fine-tuned models are reported released. Conversely, the user-study questionnaire, participant guide, and associated procedural disclosures are removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new baselines, structured datasets, probability estimation, and computational discussion. It also adds a focused explanation of differences from DPIC. The broader related-work taxonomy and prompt-inversion positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially rewritten around preliminaries, four training stages, and inference. Training-data descriptions and linguistic analysis move to appendices, experimental subsections are reorganized, and explicit contribution bullets are added. The title, author information, conclusion, and user-study terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn; the earlier in-distribution comparison table becomes a four-panel chart, and the OOD table is split into separate standard/attack tables. The ablation display becomes a substantially expanded panel figure. V2 adds algorithm and comparison tables while removing the original linguistic and user-study appendix figures.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's limited baseline coverage and makes the revised detector easier to assess through explicit fusion rules and expanded ablations. The net benefit is limited by structured tests without human-written controls, indirect DPIC comparisons, and removal of user-study materials. Numerical inconsistencies also remain: v2 Table 8 reports a Claude 3 mean of 1.0000 for entries averaging 0.9983.
